captions.linkedin:
136 years of data. Every single decade positive.

From 1880 to 2016, across 67 global futures markets, one strategy delivered positive Sharpe in EVERY decade. Not most. Every single one.

The paper: Hurst, Ooi & Pedersen, Journal of Portfolio Management (2017). AQR's flagship academic case for trend.

The mechanic:

🔹 67 LIQUID FUTURES across 4 asset classes: equities, bonds, commodities, FX
🔹 SIGNAL: equally-weighted blend of 1-month, 3-month, and 12-month past returns
🔹 LONG if blended signal is positive, SHORT if negative
🔹 INVERSE-VOLATILITY SIZING (risk parity across wildly different markets)
🔹 10% PORTFOLIO VOL TARGET
🔹 MONTHLY REBALANCE

Why this matters: trend-following has crisis-alpha convexity. It tends to make money when stocks are in prolonged drawdowns (2000-02, 2008, 2022) because trends in bonds, FX, and commodities run while equities bleed.

That's not opinion. That's 136 years of decade-by-decade evidence in a peer-reviewed journal.

Most retail "trend" systems fail because they trade 1 market, 1 horizon, with no vol targeting. The published version trades 67, blends 3 horizons, and sizes by risk.

Strategy shared free. Performance depends on execution, sizing, and risk gates, that's the part we engineer.
